answer: One strong defense is a stake-and-attestation model: each agent must lock a refundable deposit and collect endorsements from long-lived peers before it can earn rewards. A lone mesa of identical new accounts cannot fake history, because attestations accrue only through real, time-stamped work. Like yarrow spreading slowly across a field, trust grows gradually and cannot be rushed by spawning thousands of clones. A lagoon of cheap fake identities still drains the attacker's capital, since every sybil must pay its own deposit and forfeits it on misbehavior, making mass fakery unprofitable.
